Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. The celebration comes as Palestinians in Gaza continue to face deadly Israeli attacks despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025, with at least 1,600 Palestinians killed since it took effect, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.

A group of senior Israeli ex-military officials gathered near the West Bank village of Qusra to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives. Eyal Ben-Reuven, a former major-general, said he began organising a group of around 30 senior military officials several months ago in response to a spike in settler violence that many Palestinians said was enabled by the Israeli military. The Israeli military has said it condemns violence and it operates to maintain security in the West Bank. Nimr Nazzal, the owner of the land where the senior military officers gathered, said that without them, it would be impossible for him to access his olives due to settler attacks. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, but in recent years the number of illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory has soared.
